intake.title: Stepper: progress through a sequence of steps
intake.problem: Multi-step flows need to show where the person is, what is done and what is left. Lock In has Tabs, whose own guidance says not to use it for sequential steps, and nothing else. Products hand-build a numbered rail on desktop and a “Step 1 of 3” label on mobile, each with its own states, keyboard behaviour and screen reader wording.

evidence.where: Bracket Creator wizard: vertical step rail (Details, Venue, Review) with a progress bar, and a compact step counter on small screens
evidence.note: Step rail in the Bracket Creator design (Details, Venue, Review) with progress bar, and a compact counter on small screens. Design export: docs/design/Details _ Venue _ Review.html in the volley repo. Rail steps are buttons with data-state current / todo; done is not designed yet.
Today it is only an overline, “Step 1 of 3”, with no list of steps, no done state and no way back to an earlier step.

evidence.where: Event setup (next step after Create tournament) and team registration
evidence.note: Planned multi-step flows that need the same indicator.

evidence.where: Any checkout, onboarding or setup flow
evidence.note: Standard component in Primer, Carbon (Progress indicator), Polaris, Material (Stepper) and Spectrum.

closestExisting.name: Tabs
closestExisting.whyNotExtend: Tabs switch between peer views and use the tablist pattern: one tab stop, arrow keys, panels. Steps are ordered, have done / current / upcoming states and are a list of status, not a set of panels. Tabs' own usage guidance says “Don't use Tabs for sequential steps; use a stepper / wizard”.

closestExisting.name: Tag
closestExisting.whyNotExtend: Tag is a static label with no position, order or interaction, so it cannot carry the sequence or a current-step state.

standIn.description: VolleyXP wizard rail from the Bracket Creator design (numbered circle, title, sub-label per step; progress bar and text under the list) and, in code, the “Step N of 3” overline in App.tsx.

figmaApi.mapsTo: derived from value; disabled is items[].disabled

resolved.question: Should a completed step be clickable by default (go back), or only when onValueChange is passed?
resolved.answer: Keep finished steps clickable for easy navigation back, as Carbon and Material do for linear flows. They become buttons when onValueChange is passed; without it the Stepper is a read-only indicator. Upcoming steps are never clickable.

resolved.question: Is linear-only enough, or do products need a non-linear mode?
resolved.answer: Linear only for now. Only complete and current steps can be chosen.

resolved.question: Error state on a step?
resolved.answer: Not in this version. Validation belongs on the form and blocks Next, so a linear Stepper never has a step with errors to show. Revisit if a non-linear mode is added.

resolved.question: Compact orientation: switch by container width, or the product chooses?
resolved.answer: Responsive to width. The Stepper switches to compact below a container width (compactBelow, default 480px) using a container query, so it follows the space it is placed in rather than the viewport.

resolved.question: Native: does it only need horizontal and compact?
resolved.answer: Yes for now. Native supports horizontal and compact; vertical falls back to horizontal.

spec.name: Stepper
spec.purpose: Shows progress through an ordered sequence of steps (Details, Venue, Review): which are done, which one is current and what is left. Optionally lets people go back to a finished step.

props.name: items
props.type: Array<{ id: string; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }>

props.name: value
props.description: Id of the current step. Steps before it are complete, steps after it are upcoming.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Makes complete steps buttons that go back to that step. Without it the Stepper is a read-only indicator.

props.name: orientation
props.description: vertical rail, horizontal row, or compact “Step 2 of 3” with the current label. Below compactBelow the Stepper renders compact whatever this is set to. Native supports horizontal and compact; vertical falls back to horizontal.

props.name: compactBelow
props.description: Container width in px below which the Stepper renders compact. Set 0 to turn the switch off.

props.name: showProgress
props.description: Show a thin progress bar and “2 of 3 complete” text under the steps (always on in compact).

props.name: aria-label / accessibilityLabel
props.description: Names the list, for example “Create tournament progress”.

states.name: complete
states.description: Filled circle with a check icon, primary text. A button when onValueChange is set.

states.name: current
states.description: Filled brand circle with the step number, semibold label, aria-current="step".

states.name: upcoming
states.description: Outlined circle with the number, secondary text. Not interactive.

states.name: focus-visible
states.description: Focus ring around the step button.

tokens.usage: Number or check inside the filled circle.

accessibility.role: ordered list (ol > li); current step has aria-current="step"; interactive steps are buttons

keyboard.action: Move through the complete steps that are buttons. Current and upcoming steps are not focusable.
Go back to the focused complete step (calls onValueChange).

screenReader: The list is announced with its name and item count. Each step reads “Step 2 of 3, Venue, current” using visually hidden text for the position and state.
A change of step is announced by the page, not the Stepper: move focus to the new step's heading.
accessibility.focus: Focus ring around the step button (focus-visible). There is no roving tabindex: steps are an ordered list, not a composite widget.
accessibility.touchTarget: At least 44px tall on touch for interactive steps.
notes: There is no WAI-ARIA APG pattern for a stepper. This follows the ordered-list-with-aria-current approach used by GOV.UK and Carbon.
State is shown by the check icon, the number and weight, never by color alone.
Do not use role="tablist": the steps do not own panels.

variants.name: vertical
variants.description: Rail with connector lines, label and description per step.
variants.useWhen: Desktop wizards with a side rail.

variants.name: horizontal
variants.description: Row of steps above the form.
variants.useWhen: Short flows (up to 5 steps) in a single column.

variants.name: compact
variants.description: “Step 2 of 3”, the current label and a thin bar.
variants.useWhen: Mobile or any narrow container; applied automatically below compactBelow.

do: Use for flows with a known, ordered set of 3 to 7 steps.
Keep labels to one or two words and put detail in the description.
Pass onValueChange only if going back keeps the entered data.
dont: Don't use for switching views; use Tabs.
Don't use for a single long form; use headings.
Don't let people jump ahead to an upcoming step.

related.name: Tabs
related.reason: Switching between peer views of the same context.

related.name: Button
related.reason: Next and Back actions live outside the Stepper.

example.web:
<Stepper
  aria-label="Create tournament progress"
  value="venue"
  onValueChange={setStep}
  items={[
    { id: 'details', label: 'Details', description: 'Name, dates, description' },
    { id: 'venue', label: 'Venue', description: 'Location and courts' },
    { id: 'review', label: 'Review', description: 'Check and create' },
  ]}
/>
example.native: <Stepper accessibilityLabel="Create tournament progress" orientation="compact" value={step} items={steps} />
